verified: Three manual endpoints submit to the service-only queue RPC using existing tenant-bound owner/admin/ops and internal-service authorization.
Queue submission does not open sync runs, resolve provider credentials, alter mailbox progress or write source messages.
Concurrent matching submissions retain one active job; conflicting force or page-size intent is rejected without changing the saved job.
Paused capture, unavailable accounts, wrong methods and restart requests do not enqueue or reset cursors.
All three queue job types bind to the existing durable email attempt protocol.
Unknown or malformed RPC responses return unconfirmed without automatic retries or raw private diagnostics.
Frontend validates the queued contract; actual StatusPanel render distinguishes Queued, Needs attention and ordinary Success.
Connector quick actions and the internal email helper no longer interpret queue acceptance as imported message counts.
limitations: Local tests only. The SQL fixture uses recorded TEST contracts and the previously documented dependency omissions.
Requires coordinated migrations, worker/shared modules, all three endpoints and frontend release; old endpoint callers or clients expect synchronous processing.

Existing active job deduplication applies while that job is active; no permanent manual-request idempotency token is introduced. Uncertain responses require inspecting job history before resubmission.
Source eligibility at enqueue is preliminary; the worker must recheck live credential/Workspace authority before provider access.
Shared Edge TypeScript uses ambient runtime declarations, not a Deno deployment/runtime check.
No real mailbox provider requests, hosted schema changes, secrets, access grants, scheduler changes or production deployment occurred.
